text: ユーナの意思に反しても…か? / 死んじまうよりゃマシだ!
translation: Even against Yuna's wishes…huh? / It's better than dying!

vocabulary.meaning: colloquial contraction of 〜てしまう (completion, often with regret)
colloquial contraction of より + は (than; as for)

grammar: 〜に反しても uses the te-form of 反する + も (even if). 死んじまうよりゃ is heavily colloquial: 死んでしまう → 死んじまう; よりは → よりゃ.

text: 文句のある奴は前に出ろ! / 叩き出したるら!
translation: Anyone who has a complaint, step forward! / I'll knock you right out!

vocabulary.meaning: to throw out, to knock out
dialectal/rough form of 〜てやる (do for/to someone, often adversarial)

grammar: 出ろ is the imperative of 出る. 叩き出したるら is dialectal (likely Wakka's Spiran dialect): 叩き出してやる → 叩き出したる, with ら as an emphatic particle.

text: やむを得んな… / おーし!万丈一致だな!
translation: Can't be helped, I suppose… / Alright! We're all in agreement!
grammar: やむを得ん is the classical/contracted negative of やむを得る (〜ぬ negative). The phrase is a set expression meaning 'it cannot be helped.'

text: トタキ!ユーナを、ミザキョだかあさ! / ごよが!
translation: [Al Bhed dialogue — untranslatable as written; approximate intent:] Cid! Yuna — I'm counting on you to save her! / Got it!

vocabulary.meaning: Al Bhed language (cipher used by the Al Bhed people in FFX)

grammar: This line is spoken in the Al Bhed language, a substitution cipher. The text as transcribed is phonetically garbled. The meaning is inferred from context: Cid gives an order to rescue Yuna.

text: ユーナ!
translation: Yuna!

text: どこだ!?
translation: Where is she!?
grammar: Short exclamatory sentence with the copula だ. The subject (Yuna) is entirely omitted — typical of urgent spoken Japanese.

text: 聖ベベル級、エヴォンの総本山よ
translation: The holy city of Bevelle — the headquarters of Yevon.

vocabulary.meaning: head temple, headquarters (originally Buddhist; used figuratively)

grammar: よ at the end is a feminine sentence-final particle asserting information. 級 here is used as a suffix/classifier meaning 'city of that level' or simply 'the holy city.'

text: おっさん、行ってくれ! / わかってんのか、小僧? ベベルの防衛もは半端じゃねえ!
translation: Old man, take us there! / Do you understand, kid? Bevelle's defenses are no joke!
grammar: わかってんのか is an emphatic question: わかっているのか contracted colloquially. 半端じゃねえ is rough speech: じゃない → じゃねえ.

text: なんだよ、オスさん! ビビってんのか!? / そこにユーラがいる! だったら助けに行く!
translation: What's your deal, old man! Are you scared!? / Yuna is there! If so, we go save her!

vocabulary.meaning: to be scared, to freak out (colloquial)

grammar: ビビってんのか is contracted from ビビっているのか (progressive + question). 助けに行く uses the 〜に行く pattern: go for the purpose of rescuing.

text: そんだけっすよ!
translation: That's all there is to it!

vocabulary.meaning: that's all, just that (colloquial: それだけ)

grammar: そんだけ is a colloquial reduction of それだけ (only that). っすよ is a casual assertive ending combining the contracted copula っす and the particle よ.

text: フッ…不可しやがる!
translation: Heh… the damn fool's going ahead with it!

vocabulary.meaning: auxiliary verb expressing contempt or rough admiration for someone's action
impossible, unacceptable (here used loosely as 'reckless / going ahead anyway')

grammar: 〜やがる attaches to the verb stem and expresses the speaker's (often contemptuous or grudgingly impressed) attitude toward another's action. フッ is a short laugh — Auron's signature understated approval.

text: 金のベベルが!
translation: The golden Bevelle!
grammar: An exclamatory fragment. が here is an emphatic subject marker rather than a conjunction, expressing astonishment at the sight of golden Bevelle.

text: ベベルまではちょいと時間がかかる / その間に
translation: It'll take a little time to reach Bevelle. / In the meantime—

vocabulary.meaning: a little, just a bit (colloquial: ちょっと)
in the meantime, during that time

grammar: The second clause その間に is deliberately cut off, setting up the next speaker's line. まで marks the destination/limit (up to Bevelle).

text: 戦闘準備だろ!
translation: Get ready for battle, right!
grammar: だろ (contracted from だろう) at the end of a noun phrase turns it into a rhetorical confirmation: 'It's battle prep, obviously, right?'

text: なんだ!
translation: What is it!
grammar: Short exclamatory response, equivalent to 'What's going on!' The subject is omitted.

text: 内部からの攻撃です / ホームを襲ったグアードの魔物が潜り込んでいたようですな
translation: An attack from inside. / It seems the fiends from the Guado that attacked Home have snuck in.

vocabulary.meaning: it seems, it appears (inference from evidence)

grammar: 潜り込んでいたようですな combines the progressive past (〜ていた) with 〜ようだ (evidential/inferential). な at the end is a musing particle, typical of an older male speaker (here Cid or a crew member).

text: 何余裕かましやがる! / こういう正確なもので
translation: What are you being so calm about! / This is precisely the kind of thing where—

vocabulary.meaning: to act coolly/calmly, to be nonchalant (colloquial)
rough auxiliary expressing contempt for another's action

grammar: 何余裕かましやがる is an angry rhetorical question: 'Why are you being so composed?' かます is slang for 'to pull off / to put on (an attitude).' The second clause trails off, cut off by events.

text: 仕方ねえ / こうなったら / こうなったら / 船ごと爆破して / 一気に倒したるわ
translation: Can't be helped. / If it's come to this— / If it's come to this— / I'll blow up the whole ship / and take them all out in one go!

vocabulary.meaning: if it has come to this, given the situation
the ship and all, along with the ship
all at once, in one fell swoop

grammar: ごと means 'together with, including.' 一気に is an adverb of manner meaning 'in one go.' 仕方ねえ is colloquial for 仕方ない.

text: 親父は手加減ってものを知らないんだから
translation: Dad just doesn't know how to hold back.

vocabulary.meaning: to have no concept of ~, to not know what ~ is

grammar: 〜ってものを知らない is a set phrase: 'doesn't know what X is / has no concept of X.' んだから at the end expresses exasperation or resignation (explanatory んだ + から).

text: そんなことされたら / ユンナ助けに行けないでしょ
translation: If he does something like that, / we won't be able to go save Yuna, will we.

vocabulary.meaning: to be done (passive of する)
to go in order to (do something)
right?, don't you think (seeking agreement, feminine/soft)

grammar: そんなことされたら is a conditional passive: 'if that sort of thing is done (to us).' 〜に行けない = cannot go for the purpose of (rescuing). でしょ (contracted でしょう) softens the assertion.

text: 魔物は / あたしたちがやっつける
translation: We'll take care of the monsters.

vocabulary.meaning: to beat, to take out, to defeat (colloquial)

grammar: The topic (魔物は) is separated from the subject-predicate (あたしたちがやっつける) for emphasis. が marks the doer with contrastive emphasis: 'it's us who will handle them.'

text: やるっす
translation: We'll do it!

vocabulary.meaning: to do, to go for it

text: ありがとう
translation: Thank you.

text: エボン守護竜、エフレイオ、聖ベベルキを防衛する最強の聖獣よ
translation: The guardian dragon of Yevon, Evrae — the mightiest holy beast, defender of the holy city of Bevelle.
grammar: This is a noun-phrase sentence ending in よ (feminine assertion). 聖ベベルキを防衛する is a relative clause modifying 聖獣: 'the holy beast that defends holy Bevelle.'

text: 最大級の神絵だ / じゃあベベルは近いってことだな
translation: It's the ultimate-class divine creature! / So Bevelle must be close then.
grammar: 〜ってことだな is an inferential expression: 'that means/so it follows that.' な at the end is a musing/confirming particle.

text: リュック、聞こえるか? / これからあのデカボスと一戦交えるぞ
translation: Rikku, can you hear me? / We're about to go up against that big boss!

vocabulary.meaning: to engage in a battle, to have a fight

grammar: 聞こえるか is a plain-form question (rough/casual register). これから indicates immediate future. 〜ぞ is a masculine sentence-final particle for emphasis.

text: おめえらはカンパンに出て、あんにゃろを迎えるぜ
translation: You guys get out on deck and take on that bastard!

vocabulary.meaning: that bastard/guy (contraction of あいつ/あの野郎)
to receive, to go out to meet (here: to confront)

grammar: おめえら is a rough plural form of おまえ. カンパン (甲板) is the ship's deck. ぜ is a masculine emphatic sentence-final particle.

text: いいよ
translation: Sure.

text: もっと勝手に決めちゃって / 高い船賃だな
translation: Always deciding things on your own… / That's one steep fare.

vocabulary.meaning: selfishly, on one's own, without permission
colloquial て-form of 〜てしまう (expressing completion, often with mild complaint)

grammar: 決めちゃって is the te-form of 決めてしまう (contracted). もっと here expresses 'even more so / as always.' 高い船賃だな is a wry comment: they're paying for the passage by fighting.

text: 奴に近づきすぎるのは危険だ! / 近づかず離れずで戦うからな!
translation: Getting too close to it is dangerous! / We'll fight while neither too close nor too far!

vocabulary.meaning: to do too much, to be too (adjective/verb)
to distance oneself, to move away

grammar: 近づかず離れずで is a parallel negative construction using classical 〜ず: 'without getting too close and without getting too far.' It describes a middle-distance strategy.

text: 距離を変えるタイミングはお前らに任せる!
translation: I'll leave the timing of when to change distance up to you all!

vocabulary.meaning: to leave up to, to entrust

grammar: 距離を変えるタイミング is a nominalized verb phrase: 'the timing of changing distance,' using 〜る to modify the noun タイミング.

text: 早めに逃げよ! / でっかい船だ!急には動かせねえの!
translation: Give the signal to retreat early! / It's a huge ship — it can't move suddenly!
grammar: 動かせねえ is rough speech: 動かせない (potential negative) → 動かせねえ. の at the end is an explanatory/emphatic particle. 逃げよ is a volitional command form.

text: 分かった!俺が指示する!
translation: Got it! I'll give the orders!
grammar: 俺が emphasizes that Tidus himself (and no one else) will give the orders — contrastive が.

text: あたしもやるよ!
translation: I'll help too!
grammar: も adds inclusion: 'I also / I too.' よ asserts with slight energy.

text: くっ! レホス! ジョニョルダ! ドキタタスだ!
translation: [Al Bhed dialogue — untranslatable as transcribed; context: battle commands during the Evrae fight]

vocabulary.meaning: a grunt of effort or frustration

grammar: Lines appear to be Al Bhed language or distorted battle cries. The exact Al Bhed cipher cannot be confirmed from this transcription.

text: トビ! 稲田もベベルガー!
translation: [Al Bhed battle dialogue — approximate intent: Keep going! Bevelle is right there!]
grammar: As with the previous segment, this appears to be Al Bhed speech transcribed phonetically. The meaning is inferred from narrative context.

text: 偽りの花嫁を演じてまねれ / 私を医会へ送りたいと
translation: You played the part of the false bride… / Because you wanted to be sent to the next life by me.

vocabulary.meaning: to perform, to play the role of
sending to the afterlife (here likely 異界, the other realm / realm of the dead)
to send off, to see off (here: to perform the sending rite)

grammar: 〜まねれ appears to be a rough/dialectal contraction — possibly まねた/まねって (mimicked, played). 私を〜送りたいと: the と is a quotative particle, quoting Yuna's implied motive.

text: 強情な方だ それでこそ 我が花嫁にふさわしい
translation: What a stubborn one. That is precisely why you are worthy of being my bride.

vocabulary.meaning: precisely because of that, that is exactly why

grammar: それでこそ is an emphatic expression: 'that and that alone is why / precisely because of that.' Seymour's formal, archaic register (我が, 〜な方) contrasts with the other characters' speech.

text: やめー
translation: Stop—!
grammar: やめー is an elongated imperative cry: やめろ/やめて with the final vowel drawn out, conveying urgency and desperation.

text: この者どもの命 惜しくはないのか?
translation: Are their lives not precious to you?

vocabulary.meaning: these people, these fellows (slightly contemptuous plural)

grammar: 惜しくはないのか is a rhetorical negative question: 'isn't it precious?' (= 'you do care, don't you?'). は after the く-form adds emphasis/contrast.

text: 措置の選択が 仲間の命運を決める / 受け入れるか 見捨てるか
translation: Your choice of action determines the fate of your companions. / Will you accept, or will you abandon them?
grammar: 〜か〜か presents binary alternatives. 命運を決める uses the dictionary form as a present-tense clause (Seymour's formal speech). The first noun phrase 措置の選択が is the subject.

text: どちらを選ぶのだ?
translation: Which will you choose?
grammar: のだ at the end is an explanatory or emphatic construction in Seymour's formal register. It adds gravity to the question.

text: それで
translation: And so—
grammar: An incomplete connective sentence — the speaker trails off, implying what follows is understood from context (Yuna has agreed to the wedding to protect her guardians).

text: 阿姨
translation: [Unclear/non-standard transcription — possibly a cry or name called out; context: Yuna's wedding ceremony]
grammar: The text 阿姨 is Chinese characters (meaning 'auntie' in Chinese) appearing anomalously in a Japanese script. This is likely a transcription error or phonetic approximation of a Japanese word or name spoken in this moment.

text: 殺す
translation: I'll kill (you/him).
grammar: A bare dictionary-form verb used as a declaration or threat. The subject and object are both omitted — the tone and context make the intent clear (Tidus threatens Seymour).

text: 悪いな エボンの秩序のためだ / 教えに反する武器のようだな
translation: Sorry about this. It's for the order of Yevon. / Those weapons seem to go against the teachings.
grammar: 悪いな as an apology is very colloquial — a male speaker acknowledging fault without a full apology. 教えに反する is a relative clause modifying 武器 (weapons that go against the teachings).

text: 時と場合によるのだよ
translation: It depends on the time and the circumstances.

vocabulary.meaning: it depends on the time and situation (set phrase)

grammar: 時と場合による is a fixed expression. のだよ adds an explanatory tone — よ makes it slightly condescending/paternal, fitting a maester's voice.

text: やめて!
translation: Stop!
grammar: やめて is the te-form used as a request/plea: 'please stop.' More urgent and emotional than the plain imperative.

text: 武器を捨てなさい
translation: Put down your weapons.

vocabulary.meaning: to throw away, to drop, to abandon

grammar: 〜なさい is a polite but firm command, often used by authority figures or in formal situations. More authoritative than て-form requests.

text: 出ないと
translation: Or else—

vocabulary.meaning: if (you) don't ~, you must ~ (implicit threat or consequence)

grammar: 出ないと is a truncated conditional: 出ないと〔…になる〕— 'if you don't (comply), [something bad will happen].' The consequence is left unsaid for effect.

text: 私…
translation: I…
grammar: A trailing sentence — Yuna begins to speak but stops. The ellipsis conveys inner conflict and emotional weight.

text: お疲れ様でした
translation: You've worked hard. Well done.

vocabulary.meaning: thank you for your hard work (set phrase used after completing a task)

grammar: お疲れ様でした is a fixed honorific expression acknowledging someone's effort. でした (past tense) marks the task as complete. In this context it is used with bitter irony — perhaps by a Yevon official after the wedding ceremony.

text: 一緒にだろ! / 大丈夫!私も逃げるから! / やめなさい
translation: Together, right! / It's okay! I'll escape too! / Stop it!
grammar: 私も逃げるから uses 〜から at sentence end as a reassurance ('because I will escape too / so don't worry'). だろ seeks confirmation. やめなさい is a polite firm command.

text: 落ちて助かる高さではない
translation: This is not a height from which one can survive a fall.
grammar: 落ちて助かる is a te-form chain: 'to fall and survive.' This phrase modifies 高さ (height) as a relative clause: 'a height at which one can fall and survive.' ではない is a formal negative.

text: 平気だよ
translation: I'm fine.
grammar: だよ is a casual assertive ending. Yuna reassures her guardians before jumping.

text: 私は飛べる
translation: I can fly.

vocabulary.meaning: can fly (potential form of 飛ぶ)

grammar: 飛べる is the potential form of 飛ぶ. Yuna is saying she can summon an aeon to carry her — a pivotal moment where she reveals her plan to call Bahamut.

text: 信じて
translation: Trust me.
grammar: 信じて is the te-form used as a plea: 'please trust me.' A brief, emotionally charged request before Yuna jumps.

text: ユーラ!
translation: Yuna!
grammar: A cry of alarm as Yuna jumps. ユーラ is a variant of the transcription for ユウナ (Yuna) as spoken in the heat of the moment.

text: なんだ、今のは! / アルベド・ジルシの閃光弾!
translation: What was that just now! / An Al Bhed flash grenade!

vocabulary.meaning: that just now, what was just (that)

grammar: 今のは is a contracted interrogative phrase: 'what was that (just now)?' using は topicalizing 今の (the thing just now).

text: 降ろせって!チームをぶ倒してやる!
translation: Let me down, I said! I'll smash that airship to pieces!

vocabulary.meaning: to lower, to let down, to land
I said ~, I'm telling you (quotative with insistence)
to knock down forcefully, to smash (ぶ- is an intensifying prefix)

grammar: 降ろせって combines the imperative 降ろせ with って (quotative 'I said'), expressing that the speaker is repeating an order. ぶ倒す is a compound verb: ぶ (intensifier) + 倒す (to knock over).

text: 降ろさない!ユーナは逃げろと言った! / あの子と合流するのが先! / 切り抜ける!
translation: We're not landing! Yuna said to run! / Reuniting with her comes first! / We break through!

vocabulary.meaning: to join up with, to reunite
to break through, to get past

grammar: 逃げろと言った is a quotative construction with と reporting the command. 合流するのが先 uses nominalization (〜の) to make the verb phrase a noun, then が先 marks it as the priority.

text: ユーナ、どこ行ったんだろう? / ベベルキューはジーン。ユーナが目指す場所は一つ。 / イノリゴの部屋か!
translation: Where did Yuna go? / In Bevelle, there's only one place. The only place Yuna would head for. / The Chamber of the Fayth!

vocabulary.meaning: to aim for, to head toward
fayth (the beings whose prayers power aeons in FFX)

grammar: どこ行ったんだろう is introspective: 〜んだ (explanatory) + だろう (wondering). 目指す場所は一つ is a presentational sentence: 'the place she aims for is one (= only one place).'

text: 静かすぎるわね。罠。
translation: It's too quiet. A trap.
grammar: わね is a feminine sentence-final combination (わ + ね) expressing the speaker's personal feeling while seeking soft agreement. 罠 is a standalone noun — no verb needed; the implication is obvious.

text: 罠でも関係ない。ユーナが待ってんだ!
translation: Even if it's a trap, it doesn't matter. Yuna is waiting!
grammar: 〜でも is a concessive: 'even if it is a trap.' 待ってんだ is a contracted progressive + explanatory んだ: 待っているんだ — 'the fact is (she) is waiting.'

text: なんでジーンに機械があんだよ
translation: Why is there machina inside (Bevelle)?
grammar: あんだよ is a colloquial contraction of あるんだよ (explanatory んだ + よ). Wakka's disbelief at finding machina inside Yevon's holiest city is a pivotal character moment.

text: だって便利だし / そういう問題じゃねえ!教えはどうなってんだよ教えは!
translation: Well, it's convenient! / That's not the point! What happened to the teachings? The teachings!

vocabulary.word: そういう問題じゃない
vocabulary.reading: そういうもんだいじゃない
vocabulary.meaning: that's not the issue, that's not the point
what is going on with ~, what happened to ~

grammar: だって is a soft rebuttal/excuse. どうなってんだよ is contracted from どうなっているんだよ (progressive + explanatory んだ + emphatic よ). Repeating 教えは at the end is emphatic/emotional.

text: あたしに言われても困るよ
translation: Don't ask me — I have no idea what to tell you.

vocabulary.meaning: to be told by ~, for ~ to say it to me
to be troubled, to be at a loss

grammar: 〜に言われても困る is a fixed pattern: 'even if you tell me, I'm at a loss / don't ask me.' The passive 言われる with the agent に marks who is doing the telling. も is concessive: 'even if.'

text: また機械かよ / これがエヴォンの本質だ / 自らの教えを影で裏切っている
translation: Machina again! / This is the true nature of Yevon. / Betraying their own teachings in the shadows.
grammar: 影で裏切っている: 影で is a locative ('in/behind the shadows'), 裏切っている is the progressive, emphasizing that the betrayal is ongoing. Auron's calm, declarative tone underscores his foreknowledge.

text: 人を苔にしやがって
translation: Treating people like fools…

vocabulary.meaning: moss; here likely 馬鹿/コケにする — to make a fool of someone, to ridicule
to make a fool of, to mock, to treat with contempt
rough auxiliary expressing contempt for another's action

grammar: 〜にしやがって is the te-form of 〜にしやがる, expressing angry contempt: 'the nerve of them, treating people like fools.' The te-form (〜て) here indicates the reason for the speaker's anger, leaving the consequence unstated.
